chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa, who said: He narrated to me Sulayman ibn Haf al-Marwazi from the Jurist (peace be upon him)

He said: 'When a man becomes junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) during the night of Ramadan and does not perform ghusl until dawn, he must fast two consecutive months along with fasting that day, and he does not gain the merit of that day.'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became junub (state of major ritual impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for delaying ghusl until dawn in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib* clarifies that delaying ghusl until after dawn in Ramadan incurs the major expiation of fasting two consecutive months, distinct from the simple makeup of the day. Shia jurists emphasize that the missed day is not counted within the two-month period, highlighting the severity of neglecting ritual purity during the holy month. This ruling underscores the principle that intentional delay in purification, when capable, is treated similarly to breaking the fast.
